change_summary: Add CloudFront distribution for static assets (images, JS, CSS) served by storefront-service. DNS CNAME will point assets.example.com to CloudFront. Origin remains the existing S3 bucket with 1-hour cache TTL.
service_context: storefront-service is the customer-facing e-commerce frontend. Static assets currently served directly from S3 (avg 2k requests/sec). Adding CDN to reduce latency for global customers and offload origin.
deployment_plan: Phased: (1) Deploy CloudFront distribution with DNS pointing to CF but weight=0 in Route53 weighted record set. (2) Shift 10% traffic to CDN for 24h monitoring. (3) Shift to 100% after validation. Current step: deploying CF resource (weight=0, no traffic until step 2).
rollback_plan: Rollback trigger: if origin error rate > 1% or CDN cache-miss rate > 80% sustained for 10min during traffic shift. Rollback action: set Route53 weighted record to weight=0 for CloudFront (TTL=300, propagates in 5min). If CloudFront itself is unhealthy, delete CNAME record. Terraform state allows 'terraform apply' with distribution disabled.
observability_evidence: CloudFront real-time metrics in CloudWatch: requests, error rate, cache hit ratio, origin latency. Grafana dashboard: grafana.internal/d/storefront-cdn (panels: CDN hit ratio, origin bandwidth, p50/p95/p99 latency by edge location). S3 access logs enabled for origin request auditing.
alerting_evidence: New alerts added: cloudfront_5xx_rate > 1% for 5min (PagerDuty critical), cloudfront_origin_latency > 2s for 5min (PagerDuty warning), cache_hit_ratio < 50% for 30min (Slack #cdn-alerts). Existing storefront availability alert unchanged.
owner_oncall_evidence: Owner: frontend-infrastructure team. On-call: @frontend-infra-oncall PagerDuty rotation. Escalation: infra-lead (David Park) -> VP Platform. Change author: Sam Torres (frontend-infra). DNS changes reviewed by network-team.
slo_reliability_impact: storefront-service SLO: 99.9% availability, LCP < 2.5s. CDN expected to improve LCP by 30-50% for non-US users. Risk: cache misconfiguration could serve stale assets (mitigated by 1h TTL and instant invalidation capability). No error budget risk—additive improvement.
blast_radius: Static assets only (images, JS, CSS). Dynamic API requests unaffected. Initial deployment at weight=0 means zero production traffic risk. Even at 100%, worst case is CDN failure falls through to origin S3 bucket (existing path).
validation_evidence: Terraform plan reviewed: only creates new resources, no modifications to existing. ACM certificate validated (DNS validation complete). Staging environment CDN tested for 7 days with synthetic traffic: 94% cache hit ratio, p99 latency 45ms (vs 180ms origin). curl tests confirm HTTPS, headers, and cache behavior correct.
